digest.component_or_area: plan-review workflow seam tests and module size guards
propositions: No headroom guard exists on plan_review/workflow_ops.py (794 LOC) and llm/config.py (793 LOC) despite being hot files that exceed the 700 LOC policy threshold

The gate_dispatch_seam test assertion justifies itself by referencing three finalize_verdict call sites, but all three were moved to workflow_ops.py and plan_review_recovery.py; the assertion now guards a stale premise

Unregistered workflow steps cannot be detected statically because step registration depends solely on import side effects into a process-global STEP_REGISTRY dict, with no static validation layer catching a missed import
In-process assertions of step registry membership are masked by prior test imports that pre-populate STEP_REGISTRY, making a subprocess-isolated first-import check the only reliable guard form
The workflow schema treats step names as free-form strings and the linter skips validation of unknown steps by design, leaving only runtime WorkflowError to catch missing registrations
